inputs.mid_cycle_ebitdaf_derivation: FY2025 EBITDAF ($786m) is a hydrological trough (4th-lowest Waikato inflow year since 1980). Year-1 (FY2026) EBITDAF is anchored directly to management's own guidance of $1.0bn (H1-2026 actual $537m, +28% YoY on improved hydrology, tracking consistent with this guidance). Year-5 (FY2030) EBITDAF is anchored to the midpoint of management's own $1.15-1.25bn FY2030 target ($1.2bn). This is NOT a naive historical CAGR (FY2017-2025 spans a step-change acquisition of Tilt Renewables/Trustpower that makes pre/post periods non-comparable, and FY2023-2025 alone gives a MISLEADING -3.3% CAGR because it starts at a high year and ends at a trough).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: ebitdaf_5yr_cagr (post-acquisition operating series; NOT equity or EPS)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Statutory EPS and NetIncome are NOT usable growth drivers for this company: FY2023 NI=103, FY2024 NI=290, FY2025 NI=1, H1-2025 NI=-67, H1-2022 NI=427 -- these swings are driven almost entirely by non-cash fair-value movements on unhedged derivatives/carbon units plus one-off disposal gains (the $365m Tilt Renewables gain in H1-2022), not by underlying operating performance. Equity/book-value CAGR (1.0% 3yr, 5.6% 5yr) is also not a reliable growth driver here because book value is periodically stepped up by asset revaluations and was inflated by the FY2022 Tilt Renewables/Trustpower scrip-funded acquisitions rather than organic compounding. EBITDAF (management's own guided operating metric) is used instead, with pre- and post-acquisition periods explicitly NOT blended into one CAGR (FY2017-2022 predates the Tilt Renewables/Trustpower deals; FY2023-2025 is the current asset base, but a straight FY2023->FY2025 CAGR is -3.3% because FY2025 was a hydrological trough year, so it is not used as a growth rate either -- instead the DCF is anchored to management's own FY2026 EBITDAF guidance ($1.0bn) and FY2030 EBITDAF target ($1.15-1.25bn), which already embed a hydrology-normalisation view).
historical_growth.notes: SBC is immaterial for this Crown-majority utility (FY2025 SBC $0.638m on $3,498m revenue, 0.018% of revenue) so the SBC-adjustment machinery in this template is applied for completeness but has negligible effect on FCF. Reported FCF is NOT used as the DCF base or growth driver: FY2025 reported FCF was just $16m and H1-2026 was $60m, both suppressed by a growth-capex supercycle (OEC5 geothermal, Kaiwera Downs II, Kaiwaikawe wind) that is building earning assets, not destroying value -- see valuation_philosophy.

wacc_rationale.commentary: Mercury is a BBB+/Stable, Crown-majority (51%) owned NZ gentailer with a NZ$9bn+ regulated-adjacent asset base -- genuinely lower risk than the small/micro-cap NZX names in this research set, so the 15-19% stacked small-cap WACC used elsewhere in this project is NOT applied here. Build-up: NZ risk-free rate ~4.5% (10yr NZGB), equity risk premium ~6.5%, utility-appropriate beta ~0.70 (levered for gentailer hydrology/regulatory volatility, above a pure-play regulated network's ~0.5-0.6 but well below a merchant generator's >1.0) gives cost of equity ~9.05%. After-tax cost of debt ~3.96% (pre-tax ~5.5%, 28% NZ corporate tax shield) weighted at the company's actual ~47% debt / 53% equity capital structure gives a raw WACC of ~6.66%. A +0.75% premium is added for the live 'level playing field' regulatory intervention (mandatory hedge non-discrimination from ~mid-2026) plus irreducible hydrology earnings volatility that a pure DCF point-estimate cannot otherwise capture, landing on a base-case WACC of ~7.41%. Bull case (benign regulation, on-time delivery) uses WACC-0.75%; bear case (regulatory intervention bites, capex overrun, dry-year sequence) uses WACC+1.0%.

base.narrative: Mid-cycle hydrology (neither FY25 trough nor H1-26 wet-year peak), three-project build programme (OEC5, Kaiwera Downs II, Kaiwaikawe) delivered on management's own guided schedule/budget, EBITDAF path anchored to FY26 guidance ($1.0bn) ramping to FY30 target midpoint ($1.2bn), current 'level playing field' regulatory changes absorbed within the WACC premium rather than the cash flows.

bull.narrative: Sustained good-to-average hydrology, all three builds on/ahead of schedule, FY30 EBITDAF exceeds the top of guided range ($1.3bn vs $1.15-1.25bn target), benign regulatory outcome (level-playing-field rules have limited practical margin impact), continued pipeline growth beyond 2030.

bear.narrative: Dry-year sequence (a third consecutive weak hydrology year, or reversion after the H1-26 wet start), Electricity Authority 'level playing field' + possible structural-separation escalation compresses wholesale trading margin, capex overruns/delays across the three simultaneous builds keep growth capex elevated for longer while EBITDAF falls short of FY30 target, gearing drifts toward/through the top of the 2-3x target range.

entry_price.primary_hurdle_caveat: A 15% IRR hurdle is NOT a realistic entry criterion for a BBB+/Stable, regulated-adjacent utility yielding ~3.8% with a ~7.4% WACC -- no rational buyer needs 15% from an asset this defensive, so this entry price is intentionally far below both intrinsic value and the current market price. It is included only because the template requires it. The secondary entry price at approximately the company's own WACC (~9.5%, a more realistic hurdle for an income/utility holding) is the more decision-useful figure and lands much closer to both IV and the current price.

sensitivity.note: Flat rows at lower WACC values indicate the EV/EBITDAF exit-multiple cap (13x base case) is binding rather than Gordon growth -- terminal growth then has no marginal effect on intrinsic value at that WACC, which is the intended, cap-limiting behaviour.

sanity_check.methodology_note: P/E is explicitly NOT used as a valuation anchor here because statutory EPS is dominated by non-cash fair-value derivative/carbon swings (FY2025 EPS was $0.07). EV/EBITDAF (management's own guided metric) and P/B are the primary historical anchors instead.

FY2021.note: Tilt Renewables acquisition euphoria -- treated as an outlier, excluded from the cap-multiple selection

sanity_check.cap_multiple_rationale: 13x = the FY2023-2025 average, i.e. the multiple the market has actually paid for Mercury on the current (post-Tilt/Trustpower) asset base, excluding the FY2021 acquisition-euphoria spike. This is materially above the generic 8-12x gentailer range initially assumed and was corrected after computing Mercury's own 10-year trading history from Yahoo monthly closes, as instructed.

ddm_cross_check.description: A 2-stage dividend-discount model (10yr DPS path grown at the same deceleration as the DCF revenue path off the FY2026 guided 25.0cps base, terminal growth 2.25%, discounted at the 9.05% cost of equity -- no EV/EBITDAF-style cap applied) gives ~NZ$4.08/share, well below the FCF-based DCF's base-case NZ$6.95. The ~NZ$2.87 (41%) gap is the NPV of retained cash reinvested into growth capex (OEC5, Kaiwera Downs II, Kaiwaikawe) at returns management expects to exceed WACC -- this is the explicit bet embedded in the FCF-DCF's higher figure. It is a legitimate difference, not an error: the DDM only prices what shareholders are actually paid (70-85% of FCF payout policy), while the FCF-DCF also prices the retained/reinvested share. If the build programme fails to earn its cost of capital, fair value converges toward the DDM figure, not the FCF-DCF figure.

sanity_check.conclusion: Base-case IV of NZ$6.95 is +6.4% versus the current NZ$6.53 price and sits inside the stock's own 52-week range (NZ$6.08-7.16) and its recent (FY23-25) historical EV/EBITDAF band. This is the expected, boring answer for a regulated-adjacent income utility: modestly fair-to-slightly-undervalued, not a multi-bagger and not a value trap.

valuation_philosophy: Mercury is modelled as a component-built, owner-FCF DCF over a 10-year explicit horizon (not 5) because the FY2025 owner-FCF margin (a hydrological trough, further depressed by peak growth capex) is nowhere near a mature steady state -- the base-case margin only matures to ~18% by Year 10 as the three-project build programme (Ngā Tamariki OEC5, Kaiwera Downs II, Kaiwaikawe) completes and growth capex tapers from ~$430-460m/yr today toward ~$80-95m/yr by Year 10. Two corrections drive the entire model: (1) EBITDAF, not statutory EPS or reported FCF, is the operating series projected -- it is anchored directly to management's own FY2026 guidance ($1.0bn) and FY2030 target ($1.15-1.25bn midpoint $1.2bn), because FY2025's $786m reflects the 4th-lowest Waikato hydro inflow year since 1980 and is a trough, not a normal year, while H1-2026's 28% YoY EBITDAF recovery on better hydrology confirms the trough has passed; (2) capex is split into stay-in-business (~$150m/yr, grown with inflation) versus growth capex (explicitly disclosed by management, sourced from the kpis table: FY2025 growth capex $347m, H1-2026 running at an annualised ~$430-460m pace) and only the growth-capex component is tapered down over the projection as the pipeline completes post-2030 -- treating ALL capex as permanent maintenance spend would value Mercury at near zero, which is obviously wrong for a company building ~44% more generation capacity. Net debt of NZ$2,243m (company-reported, 31-Dec-2025) is subtracted once from enterprise value; it is NOT double-counted against interest income (interest income is immaterial at $1-6m/yr, well under the >1x-FCF materiality threshold, so it is left inside NOPAT without a separate strip). Terminal value uses the LOWER of Gordon growth and an EV/EBITDAF exit-multiple cap computed from Mercury's OWN 10-year trading history (13x base case, the FY2023-2025 average, excluding the FY2021 Tilt-acquisition-euphoria outlier of 22.3x) rather than the generic 8-12x gentailer range, because the actual historical data showed the market has consistently paid 13-15x since the post-acquisition asset base was assembled. Finally, this is framed explicitly as an INCOME stock: the 17-year unbroken dividend growth streak (24.0cps FY2025, 25.0cps FY2026 guided, ~3.8% gross yield at NZ$6.53) is the primary return driver for most holders, and the DCF is cross-checked against both a dividend-discount model and the stock's own NZ$6.08-7.16 52-week trading range -- not treated as a growth/multi-bagger valuation exercise.
framing_note: Mercury is fundamentally an INCOME stock, not a growth/multi-bagger opportunity: 17 consecutive years of dividend growth (24.0cps FY2025, 25.0cps FY2026 guided), a ~3.8% gross yield at NZ$6.53, and a 52-week trading range of only NZ$6.08-7.16. The realistic return profile for a holder is dividend yield plus modest real earnings/dividend growth from the generation build programme, not capital-gain-driven outsized upside. The base-case DCF result (+6.4% to intrinsic value, weighted +0.9%) is consistent with this framing: the stock is roughly fairly valued to modestly undervalued at the current price, which is the expected, unremarkable conclusion for a regulated-adjacent utility trading near its own recent historical multiple range.
